entries.14047c2d46458d27: This business makes medical supplies used in hospitals and at home, and products for pharmaceutical companies. It ranges from products used daily in hospitals, such as syringes, infusion pumps, infusion sets and infusion solutions, to products used by patients themselves, such as blood glucose monitoring systems and electronic thermometers, and contract manufacturing that fills syringes with drugs. By product group, it is divided into three subsegments: "Hospital Care Solutions," "Life Care Solutions" and "Pharmaceutical Solutions." Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥216,138 million, up 2.3% year on year. In Japan, sales rose 0.4% as the Pharmaceutical Solutions business grew, although affected by the termination of some businesses; overseas, sales rose 7.2% on increases in North America and Europe.
entries.14139d5ed670ee38: This business supports pharmaceutical companies in making medicines. In addition to contract manufacturing of prefilled syringe preparations, in which drugs are filled into syringes in advance, it handles products for pharmaceutical companies, such as syringes for filling drugs and injection needles packaged with medicines. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥49,260 million, up 10.4% year on year, the largest increase within the Medical Care Solutions Company. The company cites this business as one that supported revenue growth in Japan.

entries.227179e008c92486: This business manufactures medical devices to treat diseases of the heart, blood vessels, and blood vessels in the brain. It handles guidewires and catheters inserted into blood vessels, balloons and stents that widen blood vessels, artificial lungs and heart-lung machines used in heart surgery, and artificial blood vessels and stent grafts that replace damaged blood vessels. It is divided into four sub-segments by product group: "Interventional Systems," "Neuro," "Cardiovascular," and "Aortic." Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥676,421 million, the largest business of the company's total revenue of ¥1,131,877 million. Compared with the previous year, it rose 8.3%; overseas, all businesses grew, rising 8.6%, and in Japan, the Interventional Systems and Neuro businesses performed well, rising 5.9%.

entries.5d13fa7d692d623f: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,131,877 million, up 9.2% from the previous year. The company explains that medical demand continued to expand globally and its major businesses grew, centered on the Americas. Overseas revenue was ¥909,274 million, up 11.0% year on year, and Japan revenue was ¥222,603 million, up 2.5%. Revenue from external customers by business was ¥676,421 million for the Cardiovascular Company, ¥231,037 million for the Blood and Cell Technologies Company, ¥216,138 million for the Medical Care Solutions Company and ¥7,985 million for the Organ Technologies Business. At the Cardiovascular Company, the Interventional Systems Business grew overseas, centered on access products, and rose 8.3% from the previous year. The Blood and Cell Technologies Company posted the largest growth, up 15.4%, as its plasma innovation business expanded in North America and Global Blood Solutions performed well. The Organ Technologies Business is a reportable segment added from the current fiscal year after the company acquired all shares of Organox, Ltd. on October 29, 2025 and made it a wholly owned subsidiary, and only results from the acquisition date onward are consolidated.

entries.8e78ab18f4556798: This business makes equipment for collecting, separating and processing blood. Besides blood bags used for blood donation and transfusion, component collection systems that extract only components such as platelets and plasma from blood, centrifugal devices that separate blood components by centrifugal force, systems that automatically make blood into preparations, and systems that reduce pathogens in blood, it also handles systems for expanding cells and systems for collecting source plasma. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥231,037 million, up 15.4% year on year, the largest increase among the three existing businesses. Overseas, Global Blood Solutions performed well, up 15.5%, as the plasma innovation business expanded in North America; in Japan, sales rose 13.2% as blood collection-related products increased. No sub-segments have been established.

entries.afe3da9201c0e6a3: Customers differ by business company. In addition to hospitals, the Medical Care Solutions Company handles products that patients use themselves, such as blood glucose monitoring systems and electronic thermometers, and contract manufacturing of prefilled syringe formulations for pharmaceutical companies. The Blood and Cell Technologies Company plans to expand equipment and services that support operational efficiency at blood centers and other facilities. The Cardiovascular Company plans to propose treatment approaches suited to individual patients to physicians, based on the results of catheter treatment performed through the wrist artery (radial procedure). Part of the Medical Care Solutions Company and the Cardiovascular Company also transacts through distributors, and Terumo holds shares in 7 companies, including Toho Holdings, Alfresa Holdings and Medipal Holdings, to maintain and strengthen its distributor transaction relationships. No customer accounts for 10% or more of revenue. entries.c173884449adb51c: TERUMO CORPORATION, headquartered in Shibuya Ward, Tokyo, together with 101 [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiaries]] and 4 [[term:equity-method|equity method]] affiliates, forms a corporate group. Its business consists of 4 segments: the Cardiovascular Company, the Medical Care Solutions Company, the Blood and Cell Technologies Company and the Organ Technologies Business, and it operates an in-house company system divided by product group, with each company headquarters formulating strategies covering Japan and overseas and advancing its business accordingly. The consolidated number of employees as of March 31, 2026 was 31,185, including 17,007 at the Cardiovascular Company, 6,557 at the Blood and Cell Technologies Company and 6,331 at the Medical Care Solutions Company.

entries.ec54e46fef1c788a: What it sells are medical devices such as catheters and guidewires that pass through blood vessels, blood bags, syringes, infusion pumps and organ preservation devices, and related products. In December 2021, the company formulated a 5-year growth strategy, “GS26,” and set out a vision of “From Devices to Solutions,” aiming to become a company that goes beyond selling equipment to engage with the entire healthcare system and provide multifaceted answers to customers' challenges. Its pillars are 3 “D”s: Delivery, meaning technologies such as catheters that deliver into the body; Digital, meaning efficiency improvements and treatment optimization using data; and Deviceuticals, meaning the fusion of devices (Device) and pharmaceuticals (Pharmaceuticals). The raw plasma field of the Blood and Cell Technologies Company is cited as an example of Deviceuticals. Products are mainly made to forecast, and the filing contains no description of order records.

entries.f3b1493d87bc1963: This business makes devices for treating patients by passing thin tubes through blood vessels without making large incisions in the body. It handles guidewires and catheters that travel through blood vessels, introducer sheaths that serve as the entry point for inserting and removing catheters, devices that stop bleeding at puncture sites in arteries at the base of the leg, balloon catheters and stents that widen blood vessels, and catheters that use ultrasound to view the inside of blood vessels, among others. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥443,505 million, the largest within the Cardiovascular Company, up 9.2% year on year.
